blocks.title: The 7 times table
blocks.source:
Algoritmo Tabla
  Para i <- 1 Hasta 5 Hacer
    Escribir "7 x ", i, " = ", 7 * i;
  FinPara
FinAlgoritmo

blocks.description: A line with the values 1 to 6. The control starts at 1 and moves one by one; 5, the final value, is still included; on reaching 6 the loop ends.

caption.text: The control walks the values from the initial one to the final one, both included. When it goes past the final value, the loop ends.

The increment uses checked integer arithmetic, also after the last round: counting up to the largest integer overflows.

runs.text: The loop moves the control, not the body:

blocks.title: Changing the control inside the body
blocks.source:
Algoritmo Tocar
  Para i <- 1 Hasta 3 Hacer
    i <- i + 1;
  FinPara
FinAlgoritmo

diagnostics.message: Control variable i is modified inside the loop

blocks.title: A zero step
blocks.source:
Algoritmo Cero
  Para i <- 1 Hasta 3 Con Paso 0 Hacer
    Escribir i;
  FinPara
FinAlgoritmo

diagnostics.message: The step of a counted loop cannot be zero

runs.text: The final value and the step are kept in temporaries before starting. That is why changing, inside the body, a variable used in the header does not alter the rounds.
Ask the class to predict how many times
runs. The answer, 4 (0, 3, 6, 9), forces them to see that the final value is only included if it is reached.

points.text: declares its control and moves it by itself.
Initial, final and step are computed once.
The final value is included; the sign of the step gives the direction.
A zero step is a failure; touching the control, an error.
